correctness.rationale: The full Fourier-band decomposition has dimensions 1+n+n(q-2). Conditional hypergeometric covariance on the uniform k-subset of active coordinates gives the radial contrast eigenvalue U, symbol-balanced transverse covariance gives T, and the constant-plus-radial-sum Gram is a rank-one 2x2 block with eigenvalues R and 0. Multiplication by the exact shell density w gives the concentration spectrum and the shell-equation kernel. Direct symbolic subtraction yields \(R-T=z(z-1)/[n(q-1)]\), \(R-U=(z-1)(z+q-1)/[(n-1)(q-1)]\), \(T-U=qk(z-1)/[n(n-1)(q-1)]\), with \(z=qk-(q-1)n\), so positive-eigenvalue equality iff z=1. Actual character matrices are computationally checked for 18 finite parameter triples and exact Fraction arithmetic tests the resonance across \(3\le q\le15\), \(2\le n\le79\), and interior \(k\); finite experiments are not the proof.

value.rationale: A full fixed-weight Hamming sphere is a canonical sampling set in finite Fourier analysis. The theorem completely determines the nonzero singular values, dimension-one unavoidable kernel, sharp stable interpolation after quotient, and an infinite precisely congruence-classified family of optimally conditioned frames. The q-ary transverse symbol modes and arithmetic equalization are a meaningful structural distinction from Boolean ball or degree-two shell examples. The natural entire-infinite-family classification, not the elementary covariance identity alone, supplies value.
